Cash is $259. Both owned properties are mortgaged. St. James Place is needed to complete the orange set. It is owned by p4. A trade offer to p2 was rejected. Unmortgage costs are too high without that property. Selling both oranges is also avoided.

I cannot acquire the full orange monopoly through a trade. The only remaining path is buying St. James Place directly for cash.

I will offer p4 $250 for St. James Place, leaving only $9 in cash. Unmortgaging both properties costs roughly $210, so I cannot afford to build without that trade.

The $250 offer would leave only $9, which is insufficient to unmortgage both properties and build. The orange monopoly would be useless until more cash is collected. The bluff failed because p2 rejected the counter without bidding for St. James. I will end the turn instead of making a bad trade.

I am now calculating the next roll from Tennessee Avenue. A 7 would hit Illinois, where p2 has no houses and pays $20 rent. An 8 would hit B&O with three railroads and pay $100. I am also checking whether p4 owns Atlantic without a full orange monopoly.

p4 owns the green set: Atlantic, North Carolina, and Pennsylvania. Unbuilt greens double rent. The next roll from Tennessee Avenue is relatively safe with only modest rents. I will end the turn without unmortgaging.
